content:
sasha: Heads-up — I hit a weird one with the async Python client and streaming + retries. After a transient 502 the client retried and the app received duplicated partial chunks, e.g. 'Hello', 'Hello world' where 'Hello' got replayed mid-stream.
kevin: ugh. do you have a small repro or logs? sounds like replaying a buffered chunk rather than resuming.
sasha: Yep. Minimal repro in a quick script: client.stream(..., idempotency_key='evt-123') as gen: async for chunk in gen: process(chunk)
sasha: When the upstream 502 happens, the retry logic reconstructs the stream from the buffer and re-emits the last N tokens instead of resuming at a continuation boundary.
kevin: can you paste the stack / log snippet? also which sdk version?
sasha: sdk 0.8.3. log snippet:

```
WARNING:redwood.client.retry:transient 502, retrying attempt=1 backoff=0.41s
DEBUG:redwood.client.stream:replaying buffered chunk size=128 last_token_index=523
ERROR:app.stream-consumer:duplicate partial chunk received, state mismatch
Traceback (most recent call last):
  File "app/consumer.py", line 87, in _drain
    await handler.on_message(chunk)
ValueError: duplicate partial chunk
```

sasha: Repro script: https://github.com/redwood-inference/sdk/tree/main/examples/async-replay-repro (PR linked below)
elaine: interesting. are you using the same idempotency key across retries? streaming is tricky — idempotency semantics are for whole-request side effects, not for streamed partials.
ben: Iirc the current retry path treats streaming like unary and just replays buffered bytes. That was a fast startup implementation but it's not semantically safe for clients that rely on contiguous stream state.
elaine: suggest we add an opt-in failure mode for streams: either (A) mark streams as non-replayable by default, or (B) surface a 'stream_resume_token' that server can provide to continue safely.
kevin: +1 for making streams non-replayable by default. Breaking change though, need migration guidance and a quickstart example showing how to handle reconnects (idempotency for side-effects vs resume tokens for content).
sasha: For the short term I'd like a fix that prevents duplicate partials — maybe detect if the handler has consumed any bytes and refuse to replay; emit a special error so apps can decide to restart the whole op.
ben: Implementation idea: expose RetryPolicy.safe_to_replay_streams: bool and a RetryPolicy.async_backoff coroutine that uses asyncio.sleep with decorrelated jitter. Also add a 'suppress_replay_for_streams' flag on the client config.
kevin: from a typing/SDK DX POV we should type RetryPolicy as a Protocol so users can implement custom policies easily and mypy will be happy. Right now RetryPolicy is just a dict in the codebase which makes extension awkward.
elaine: +1. also add typed overloads for stream(...) returning AsyncGenerator[StreamChunk, None] so IDEs show chunk types. current Any everywhere.
devex-bot: CI alert — example/async-replay-repro failed flake8 in PR #2423 (https://github.com/redwood-inference/sdk/pull/2423)
ben: I started a sketch PR to default suppress replay for streams and add a warning: https://github.com/redwood-inference/sdk/pull/2431 — it also adds RetryPolicy Protocol + typed backoff signature. need reviewers.
sasha: thanks. two product-ish questions: (1) do we want resume tokens as a roadmap item? (2) should the quickstart sample app demonstrate an authoritative pattern (restart entire session on any retry) for newcomers?
elaine: Resume tokens are ideal but require server/contract changes. For now quickstart should show an explicit "no replay" pattern and provide a small helper decorator: @no_stream_replay that sets idempotency semantics and logs guidance.
kevin: agree. for SDK parity we should document JS/Python behavior parity: both should have suppress_replay_for_streams and matching typing docs.
ben: I'll land the 'no replay by default' toggled behind a config flag and add the Protocol for RetryPolicy. can we schedule a short design review tomorrow 10:30? I'll post a short RFC with examples.
sasha: sounds good. assigning followups: ben -> implement flag + types, elaine -> quickstart sample update + copy, kevin -> coord JS parity and docs. I'll paste the repro link and sample logs into the issue.
sasha: thanks everyone :handshake:
